selected_mathematical_checks: The complete source packet parametrization averages uniformly over maximal hull ideal classes and local labels, with signs and orbit volume accounted for by the unit fundamental domain. Therefore a full hull-class coset of index k has mass exactly 1/k. Local saturation index q differs from the label count; neither is silently replaced by a multiplier-order index.

The character-retaining unfolding carries chi(I)=chi([a])^(-1), since a=(alpha)I^(-1). Its normalization remains 1/(sqrt(D) kappa). Finite absolute untwisted integrability justifies the twisted sum. This is a one-vector Siegel-transform identity, not an identity for arbitrary compact tests.

Splitting an ideal into S-supported and coprime parts gives the fractional divisor bound with coefficient P(v)/d(v). The exact shell identity sums that coefficient to Z_S/q. This preserves the necessary q^(-1) uniformity for arbitrary local type; dropping probabilities before summation would not.

The cube product-fiber logarithmic volume has coefficient 2^n/(n-1)!. Differentiating in the sup-radius and substituting t=z^(1/n)exp(u) gives the convergent gamma integral with coefficient 2^n n^(n-1)/p^(n-1). A shortest vector contributes H^p to the positive Siegel test on H>R0.

At U=Q^(3/4), the small-norm contribution has Q exponent -(1-p/n)/4 after multiplication by Q^(p/n)/(sqrt(D) kappa) and the shell normalization. Above U, the source cumulative count gives the R0^(p-n) contribution. If Q/R0^n<U, the upper range is empty; no extra R0-dependent analytic threshold is used.

Z_S is bounded by a constant times q^epsilon for each positive epsilon, including arbitrary ramification. Together with the supplied reciprocal residue bound and q<=Q this leaves the displayed Q^(-(1-p/n)/8) error after logarithms. The conclusion concerns moments below n and does not cover the endpoint n or higher-rank cusp observables.

The additive B_p(Q) error in UI145 should be used with a slightly larger p-prime<n for uniform tail truncation: it supplies a uniform p-prime moment for large Q, hence a tail tending to zero for the lower p at fixed growing cutoff. Individual finite packet supports are compact. Thus the stated full-packet uniform integrability and convergence of continuous H^p-dominated tests are paid, not inferred from weak convergence alone.

Domination by k gives RUI, and the chosen R0=k^(2/(n-p)) gives a tail O(1/k+k B_p(Q)). With d<=Q^(2n), delta<(1-p/n)/(16n) makes the second term vanish. This is only a growing-cutoff statement and does not prove fixed-cutoff tightness for every polynomial-index coset.

For each fixed time T, the squared centered orbit average is compactly supported plus a constant. Full-packet convergence handles that fixed test. Haar ergodicity follows from invariance under contracted root unipotents for a regular diagonal element. Taking the packet limit before T tends to infinity proves bounded-index transfer, but provides no polynomial-index rate.

Character orthogonality proves C1 and C2 with the inverse character convention. Jensen applied first within each hull measure and then across a coset gives C4 uniformly over all subgroups, with no index loss in the average. Chebyshev yields a vanishing proportion of bad cosets, not control of every coset.

For unbounded H^p-dominated tests, the mean of coset tail integrals equals the full-packet tail exactly. Fixed compact truncation plus the full-packet moment result proves C5 in mean absolute value. An unrestricted L2 claim is not made when the required higher moment is unavailable.

The finite single-bad-class example has variance tending to zero and worst deviation tending to one. It correctly tests the mean-to-maximum interface only, not the actual arithmetic target. The sufficient Fourier square-sum condition o(1/k) is stronger than the proved o(1).

The source ordinary-ball estimate is obtained for fixed radius before the packet limit, with a radius-dependent threshold. Its dominated-component entropy argument uses domination by a fixed finite constant and a probability limit. Neither fact automatically survives growing k; any entropy route must pay shrinking-radius dependence, fixed-cutoff no escape and every ergodic component.
